item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Nov 18, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: Using Grok Bot to Recover Websites While I Sleep + 2026 Year-End Review — Thu Nov 19, 7:00 PM
item.description:
WordPress Lancaster This month, **Austin Ginder** will show how he uses **Grok Bot**, a team of AI routines, to watch and repair WordPress sites overnight. Every 30 minutes, a down-site watcher checks for outages, connects over SSH and works out what broke. When the cause is bad code, it fixes it and writes up what it changed. In its first nine days it patched about a dozen live sites, mostly while Austin was asleep.
**What we'll cover:**
* How the watcher sorts an outage: fixable, not ours, or hands off * The fix order: update, roll back, patch, and deactivate only as a last resort * Real fixes from the past month, including PHP 8 fatals, a Gravity Forms class change and a disabled PHP function * The steps after every fix: back up, purge cache, confirm the site loads, and log the change * Reviewing security signals the same way: an overnight run covered 226 findings across 206 sites * The guardrails, what it still gets wrong, and why it runs on Austin's Mac for now

item.title: Geminids Meteor Shower at Millport Conservancy — Sun Dec 13, 6:00 PM — Millport Conservancy
item.description: [vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”128240″] Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year! Join us at Millport Conservancy on the night of Sunday, December 13th, to observe what could be the most spectacular meteor shower of the year! Far from the city lights of Lancaster, the darker skies of Millport mean we could see up to 30+ meteors, if the weather cooperates! The Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year, and are considered one of the two best showers for viewing (along with August’s Perseids). The Geminids are unlike most other meteor showers, in that they are not likely caused by a debris field from a comet. Instead, the Geminids have been identified as being spawned from the debris field of 3200 Phaethon, which is what seems to be an asteroid. item.description:

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: C. Emlen Urban & The Chocolate King — Thu Nov 19, 5:30 PM — LancasterHistory Museum & Research Center
item.description:
One built an empire with a Kiss and the other designed it. This is the untold story of Milton S. Hershey and his architect, C. Emlen Urban. What drove these two men to achieve goals and fame beyond their wildest dreams? Why is one an American icon and the other unknown beyond his hometown? Drawn from his new book, Urban and the Chocolate King, architect and historian Gregg Scott joins LancasterHistory to tell the tale of two men who met as young boys in the small town of Lancaster, PA, and began a journey of design and construction that endured for fifty years.
Gregg Scott is a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects, a partner emeritus and co-founder of RLPS Architects, a monthly columnist for LNP, and twice recipient of the Journalist and Educators Award presented by the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County. Most recently, the author of Urban Legend, Urban Alphabet, and the 2026 fall release of Urban and the Chocolate King.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lanc
